382	### Step C1 — three pure helpers *(no dependency on A or B — parallelisable)*
383	
384	**Changes** — all in `overrides/app/utils/`:
385	
386	**`regionPrefCookie.ts`** — contract, spec only what's specified:
387	
388	```
389	zimm-region-pref=1|l=<epochSeconds>|c=<epochSeconds>
390	path=/; samesite=lax; secure; max-age=<long>
391	```
392	
393	`l` = language prompt dismissed/acted, `c` = country prompt. **No `s` flag** — nothing specifies
394	storing a manual selection; the `1|` version prefix means adding one later strands nothing. Exports
395	a named `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS = 7` constant. **Parse and serialise must be pure and
396	isomorphic** (zero `document` reference), with thin client `get`/`set` on top — the client writes it
397	and the server will later read it from the `Cookie` header in `request-processor.js`. One module,
398	four eventual consumers (689, 823, 688, 817); otherwise 817 re-implements the parser and the two
399	drift. `try/catch` on **read and write** (Safari private mode throws on *read* — see
400	`useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:30`), plus an SSR guard (`typeof document === 'undefined'`). Not
401	`httpOnly`.
402	
403	**`crossSiteUrl.ts`** — strip the base path and the current site alias, then
404	`buildUrl(path, targetAlias, targetLocale)`. `getPathWithLocale` cannot be reused: it swaps the
405	locale *within one site*, and the four EU languages are separate **sites**. Preserve the path, drop
406	`refine` (`disallowParams: ['refine']`), matching `footer/index.jsx:152`. Returns a string; the
407	caller performs the hard navigation.
408	
409	**`shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts`** — pure predicate:
410	
411	```ts
412	shouldShowLanguagePrompt({ sfccSiteId, currentLanguage, browserLanguages, suppressedAt, now })
413	  : { show: boolean; targetLanguage?: string }
414	```
415	
416	Gate is `sfccSiteId === 'ZimmermannEU'` — one comparison covering all four EU domestic PWA sites and
417	naturally excluding EU International (`ZimmermannEUIntl`, English-only). **Match on the primary
418	subtag, both sides**: browsers report `fr-FR`, `it-CH`, `en-AU`; our site locales are `fr`, `it`,
419	`es`, `en-GB`. `fr-FR`→`fr` and our `en-GB`→`en`, or a French shopper reporting `fr-FR` never
420	matches and the prompt silently never fires. Read-time window enforcement, not browser expiry.
421	
422	Plus a `.test.ts` beside each.
423	
424	**Pass criteria**
425	
426	- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.

Plus the primary-subtag cases `fr-FR`→`fr` and `en-GB`→`en`.
434	- [ ] Pure functions, no side effects, no imports from `overrides/app/hooks/` (utilities must not depend on hooks — the dependency runs the other way).

437	two assertions, confirm red, revert. The window-lapsed and primary-subtag cases specifically: those
438	are the two that would pass trivially against a stub.

# Build Plan — SFCC-831 + SFCC-689

> Produced by `zm-planner` 2026-09-12, synthesising the full decision record in
> `./decisions.md` and `../SFCC-689/decisions.md` (both authoritative — every decision in them
> was taken with Marcel in session and must not be re-litigated during the build).
> Original gate: `./findings.md`. Superseded 2026-09-09 run: `./findings-2026-09-09.md`.
>
> **Invoke as `zimmerMANNBuild SFCC-831`** — one branch, one PR, both stories.

**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (clean, on `develop` @ `2510cea`)

**Verified baseline, captured 2026-09-12 before any change:**

| Gate | Baseline |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | exit 0, no output |
| `npm run test` | **76 files / 1164 tests / 0 failures**, ~29s |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | **"3 unacknowledged violation(s) found."** (pre-existing, untouched by this work) |
| `git status` | clean |

Every pass criterion below is written against those four numbers. They are the only honest
definition of "didn't break anything."

---

## 1. Goal statement

Build the EU country/language mismatch prompt as prescribed by **SFCC-831** (the presentational
component) and **SFCC-689** (the trigger that consumes it), as designed in Figma component
symbols `40002103:7407` / `40002104:10184` / `40002104:10133` (location) and `40002431:38549` /
`:38533` / `:38575` (language), as approached by the FED handbook's co-located-recipe and
container/presentational rules, as established by `zimmProductCard` (discriminated-union
`VARIATION_CONFIG` dispatch) and `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (drawer composition), using a **new
`Zimm`-namespaced theme recipe plus a new opt-in `prompt` size on the existing shared
`ZimmDrawer` atom** — not a new drawer shell and not a foundation-token change. Done means: a
shopper on `/it-eu/` whose browser reports French sees a modal drawer, in the storefront's own
language, offering to switch to `/fr-eu/`; acting or dismissing writes a 7-day `zimm-region-pref`
cookie at `path=/` before a hard navigation; and the prompt never fires again inside that window,
on any EU path. Both stories ship in **one branch, one PR**, with the drawer's incidental defect
fixes named and attributed in the PR body.

---

## 2. Scale call — one branch, eight commits, and a deliberately trimmed loop

**One branch, one PR, eight commits.** This is a single coherent feature with one reviewer
audience: SFCC-689 is unbuildable without SFCC-831, and SFCC-831 has no consumer without
SFCC-689. Splitting them creates a PR that ships dead code and a second PR that can't be reviewed
without the first. Marcel already decided this; the commit boundaries below are what make it
reviewable anyway.

**Commit boundaries** (the `commit-msg` hook enforces conventional commits; the PR *title* stays
plain-conventional with no SFCC key, per the accepted-PR standard):

| # | Subject |
|---|---|
| 0 | *(no commit — install + baseline)* |
| A1 | `feat(drawer): SFCC-831 add prompt size and narrow-panel width floor` |
| A2 | `fix(a11y): SFCC-831 localise ZimmDrawer close button label` |
| B1 | `feat(regional): SFCC-831 add country/language mismatch prompt component` |
| B2 | `chore(contentful): SFCC-831 seed regional prompt uiCopy keys` |
| C1 | `feat(regional): SFCC-689 add region cookie, cross-site URL and eligibility helpers` |
| C2 | `fix(regional): SFCC-689 match useCountryConfig on sfccSiteId` |
| C3 | `feat(regional): SFCC-689 show EU language prompt on first visit` |

The A1/A2 split is not cosmetic. It is how the reviewer sees, from `git log` alone, that the
`prompt` size serves SFCC-831 and the close-label fix serves four unrelated consumers. That is the
framing a separate PR would have given, at zero process cost.

### How much loop this actually warrants

Full loop (implement → test → scope-check → score) on **A1, B1, C1, C3** only. These four carry
all the new logic, all the new test files, and the only Tier 2 mount.

**Deliberately dropped, and why:**

- **No `useLanguagePrompt` hook.** The container in C3 has one `useState` and one `useEffect`; all
  the branching lives in the already-unit-tested pure predicate. `components.md`'s
  extract-to-hook threshold is not met. If the container exceeds ~80 lines during implementation,
  extract then — do not pre-build it.
- **No E2E / Playwright spec, and no `.feature` file.** Two independent reasons: the gherkin-first
  workflow forbids writing a spec before Lead QA signs off a `.feature`, and adding a `regional`
  area to the change-scoped E2E allow-list means editing `.github/workflows/qa.yml`, which is
  **Tier 1**. Out of scope; see the closing note for the consequence.
- **No `npm run test:max-file-size` per step.** It runs a full production build.
  `ZimmDrawer`/`ZimmButton`/`ZimmIcon` are already in the `_app` chunk via header and footer, so
  the marginal bundle cost is near zero. Run it once at the end only if the Test-tier gate

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

37	    const params = new URLSearchParams(search)

1	/*

7	
8	import {getConfig} from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config'
9	import {getRouterBasePath} from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/utils'
10	
11	/**
12	 * This functions takes an url and returns a site object,
13	 * an error will be thrown if no url is passed in or no site is found
14	 * @param {string} url
15	 * @returns {object} site - a site object
16	 */
17	export const resolveSiteFromUrl = (url) => {
18	    if (!url) {
19	        throw new Error('URL is required to find a site object.')
20	    }
21	    const {pathname, search} = getPathnameAndSearch(url)
22	    const path = `${pathname}${search}`
23	    let site
24	
25	    // get the site identifier from the url
26	    const {siteRef} = getParamsFromPath(path)
27	    const sites = getSites()
28	
29	    // step 1: use the siteRef to look for the site from the sites in the app config
30	    // since alias is optional, make sure it is defined before the equality check
31	    site = sites.find((site) => site.id === siteRef || (site.alias && site.alias === siteRef))
32	    if (site) {
33	        return site
34	    }
35	
36	    //Step 2: if step 1 does not work, use the defaultSite value to get the default site
37	    site = getDefaultSite()
38	    // Step 3: throw an error if site can't be found by any of the above steps
39	    if (!site) {
40	        throw new Error(
41	            "Can't find a matching default site. Please check your sites configuration."
42	        )
43	    }
44	    return site
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * Returns the default site based on the defaultSite value from the app config
49	 * @returns {object} site - a site object from app config
50	 */
51	export const getDefaultSite = () => {
52	    const {app} = getConfig()
53	    const sites = getSites()
54	
55	    if (sites.length === 1) {
56	        return sites[0]
57	    }
58	
59	    return sites.find((site) => site.id === app.defaultSite)
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * Return the list of sites that has included their respective aliases
64	 * @return {array} sites - list of sites including their aliases
65	 */
66	export const getSites = () => {
67	    const {sites = [], siteAliases = {}} = getConfig().app || {}
68	
69	    if (!sites.length) {
70	        throw new Error("Can't find any sites from the config. Please check your configuration")
71	    }
72	
73	    return sites.map((site) => {
74	        const alias = siteAliases[site.id]
75	        return {
76	            ...site,
77	            ...(alias ? {alias} : {})
78	        }
79	    })
80	}
81	
82	/**
83	 * Given a site reference, return the site object
84	 * @param siteRef - site reference to look for the site object
85	 * @returns {object | undefined} found site object or default site object
86	 */
87	export const getSiteByReference = (siteRef) => {
88	    const defaultSite = getDefaultSite()
89	    const sites = getSites()
90	
91	    return (
92	        sites.find((site) => {
93	            return site.alias === siteRef || site.id === siteRef
94	        }) || defaultSite
95	    )
96	}
97	
98	/**
99	 * Remove the base path from a path string only when path equals basePath or path starts with basePath + '/'.
100	 * @param {string} path - the path to strip
101	 * @param {string} basePath - the base path to remove
102	 * @returns {string} the path with base path removed, or the original path
103	 */
104	export const removeBasePathFromPath = (path, basePath) => {
105	    if (!basePath) return path
106	    if (path.startsWith(basePath + '/') || path === basePath) {
107	        return path.substring(basePath.length) || '/'
108	    }
109	    return path
110	}
111	
112	/**
113	 * This function return the identifiers (site and locale) from the given url
114	 * The site will always go before locale if both of them are presented in the pathname
115	 * @param path {string}
116	 * @returns {{siteRef: string, localeRef: string}} - site and locale reference (it could either be id or alias)
117	 */
118	export const getParamsFromPath = (path) => {
119	    let {pathname, search} = getPathnameAndSearch(path)
120	
121	    // Remove the base path from the pathname if present since
122	    // it shifts the location of the site and locale in the pathname
123	    const basePath = getRouterBasePath()
124	    pathname = removeBasePathFromPath(pathname, basePath)
125	
126	    const config = getConfig()
127	    const {pathMatcher, searchMatcherForSite, searchMatcherForLocale} = getConfigMatcher(config)
128	    const pathMatch = pathname.match(pathMatcher)
129	    const searchMatchForSite = search.match(searchMatcherForSite)
130	    const searchMatchForLocale = search.match(searchMatcherForLocale)
131	
132	    // the value can only either in the path or search query param, there will be no overridden
133	    const siteRef = pathMatch?.groups.site || searchMatchForSite?.groups.site
134	
135	    const localeRef = pathMatch?.groups.locale || searchMatchForLocale?.groups.locale
136	    return {siteRef, localeRef}
137	}
138	
139	/**
140	 * This function returns the url config from the current configuration
141	 * @return {object} - url config
142	 */
143	export const getUrlConfig = () => {
144	    const {app} = getConfig()
145	    if (!app.url) {
146	        throw new Error('Cannot find `url` key. Please check your configuration file.')
147	    }
148	    return app.url
149	}
150	
151	/**
152	 * Given your application's configuration this function returns a set of regular expressions used to match the site
153	 * and locale references from an url.
154	 * @param config
155	 * @return {{searchMatcherForSite: RegExp, searchMatcherForLocale: RegExp, pathMatcher: RegExp}}
156	 */
157	export const getConfigMatcher = (config) => {
158	    if (!config) {
159	        throw new Error('Config is not defined.')
160	    }
161	
162	    const allSites = getSites()
163	    const siteIds = []
164	    const siteAliases = []
165	    const localesIds = []
166	    const localeAliases = []
167	    allSites.forEach((site) => {
168	        siteAliases.push(site.alias)
169	        siteIds.push(site.id)
170	        const {l10n} = site
171	        l10n.supportedLocales.forEach((locale) => {
172	            localesIds.push(locale.id)
173	            localeAliases.push(locale.alias)
174	        })
175	    })
176	    const sites = [...siteIds, ...siteAliases].filter(Boolean)
177	    const locales = [...localesIds, ...localeAliases].filter(Boolean)
178	
179	    // prettier-ignore
180	    const searchPatternForSite = `site=(?<site>${sites.join('|')})`
181	    // prettier-ignore
182	    // eslint-disable-next-line
183	    const pathPattern = `(?:\/(?<site>${sites.join('|')}))?(?:\/(?<locale>${locales.join("|")}))?(?!\\w)`
184	    // prettier-ignore
185	    const searchPatternForLocale = `locale=(?<locale>${locales.join('|')})`
186	    const pathMatcher = new RegExp(pathPattern)
187	    const searchMatcherForSite = new RegExp(searchPatternForSite)
188	    const searchMatcherForLocale = new RegExp(searchPatternForLocale)
189	    return {
190	        pathMatcher,
191	        searchMatcherForSite,
192	        searchMatcherForLocale
193	    }
194	}
195	
196	/**
197	 * Given a site and a locale reference, return the locale object
198	 * @param site - site to look for the locale
199	 * @param localeRef - the locale ref to look for in site supported locales
200	 * @return {object|undefined}
201	 */
202	export const getLocaleByReference = (site, localeRef) => {
203	    if (!site) {
204	        throw new Error('Site is not defined. It is required to look for locale object')
205	    }
206	    return site.l10n.supportedLocales.find(
207	        (locale) => locale.id === localeRef || locale.alias === localeRef
208	    )
209	}
210	
211	/**
212	 * Determine the locale object from an url
213	 * If the localeRef is not found from the url, set it to default locale of the current site
214	 * and use it to find the locale object
215	 *
216	 * @param url
217	 * @return {Object} locale object
218	 */
219	export const resolveLocaleFromUrl = (url) => {
220	    if (!url) {
221	        throw new Error('URL is required to look for the locale object')
222	    }
223	    let {localeRef} = getParamsFromPath(url)
224	    const site = resolveSiteFromUrl(url)
225	    const {supportedLocales} = site.l10n
226	    // if no localeRef is found, use the default value of the current site
227	    if (!localeRef) {
228	        localeRef = site.l10n.defaultLocale
229	    }
230	    const locale = supportedLocales.find(
231	        (locale) => locale.alias === localeRef || locale.id === localeRef
232	    )
233	    if (locale) {
234	        return locale
235	    }
236	    // if locale is not defined, use default locale as fallback value
237	    const defaultLocale = site.l10n.defaultLocale
238	    return supportedLocales.find(
239	        (locale) => locale.alias === defaultLocale || locale.id === defaultLocale
240	    )
241	}
242	
243	/**
244	 * Extract pathname and search params from a given url
245	 * @private
246	 * @param url
247	 * @returns {{search: (string|string), pathname: string}}
248	 */
249	function getPathnameAndSearch(url) {
250	    // since url is a partial url, we pass in a dummy domain to create a validate url to pass into URL constructor
251	    const {pathname, search} = new URL(url, 'https://www.some-domain.com')
252	    return {pathname, search}
253	}
254	
255	/**
256	 * Extract Page Designer parameters from a given URL.
257	 * These parameters are used when previewing pages in Page Designer edit mode.
258	 * @param {string} url - The URL to extract parameters from
259	 * @returns {{mode?: string, pdToken?: string, pageId?: string}} - Page Designer parameters
260	 */
261	export const resolvePageDesignerParamsFromUrl = (url) => {
262	    if (!url) {
263	        return {}
264	    }
265	    const {search} = getPathnameAndSearch(url)
266	    const searchParams = new URLSearchParams(search)
267	
268	    const params = {}
269	    const mode = searchParams.get('mode')
270	    const pdToken = searchParams.get('pdToken')
271	    const pageId = searchParams.get('pageId')
272	
273	    if (mode) {
274	        params.mode = mode
275	    }
276	    if (pdToken) {
277	        params.pdToken = pdToken
278	    }
279	    if (pageId) {
280	        params.pageId = pageId
281	    }
282	
283	    return params
284	}

13	// See config/sites.js for how the two are merged.
14	//
15	// When adding a country/locale:
16	//   1. Add an entry here (id, optional sfccSiteId, locales[].alias).
17	//   2. Run `npm run sync:regional-config` — this regenerates
18	//      sites.generated.js, countries.generated.ts, and
19	//      contentfulMapping.generated.ts from Business Manager in one pass (the
20	//      site must already exist in BM). Do NOT hand-edit locale/currency data
21	//      in countries.ts or contentfulMapping.ts — it's derived now.
22	//   3. Add the new slug's business-logic entry to COUNTRY_OVERLAY in
23	//      overrides/app/config/countries.ts (shippingCountry, checkoutOwner,

26	//   4. If it needs e2e coverage, add it to e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js too.

1	/**
2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
3	 *
4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
10	 *
11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
13	 */
14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
22	
23	/**
24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
25	 *
26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
30	 *
31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
33	 */
34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
35	
36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
37	
38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);
40	
41	/**
42	 * A single leading `/` is a same-origin relative path that needs the current site/locale prefix
43	 * from `useMultiSite()`'s `buildUrl()` (see `buildSafeHref`/`useSafeHref`) before it's safe to
44	 * navigate to — an unprefixed internal path always falls back to the default site.
45	 *
46	 * Checks the normalised value, same as `isSafeHref` — a raw, un-normalised check would disagree
47	 * with `isSafeHref` on a value like a leading-space href (`normalise` strips it, `isSafeHref`
48	 * allows it), misclassifying a real internal path as external and silently skipping `buildUrl`.
49	 *
50	 * Relies on `isSafeHref` having already run: that regex's own negative lookahead is what keeps
51	 * `//host`/`/\host` (off-site authority references) out of this function's input in practice, so
52	 * this check only needs to distinguish "internal path" from the other forms `isSafeHref` allows
53	 * (`https?:`, `tel:`, `mailto:`, `#fragment`) — every one of which must NOT be run through
54	 * `buildUrl` (it would corrupt an absolute/external URL, or replace an in-page fragment's own
55	 * page path with just the site prefix).
56	 */
57	export const isInternalHref = (href: string): boolean => normalise(href).startsWith('/');
58	
59	/**
60	 * Runs `href` through `buildUrl()` only when it's an internal path (see `isInternalHref`) —
61	 * every other form `isSafeHref` allows is returned unchanged, exactly as given (not normalised —
62	 * normalising an external/tel/mailto/# value isn't this function's job). `buildUrl` itself
63	 * receives the *normalised* internal path, not the raw one, so a leading-space href doesn't leak
64	 * a stray character into the prefixed URL. `buildUrl` is passed in rather than looked up here
65	 * since this module has no hook of its own; see `useSafeHref`
66	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useSafeHref.ts`) for the hook form of this same composition, and for the
67	 * single place every internal-navigation call site in this app should reach for.
68	 */
69	export const buildSafeHref = (href: string, buildUrl: (path: string) => string): string => {
70	  const normalisedHref = normalise(href);
71	  return isInternalHref(normalisedHref) ? buildUrl(normalisedHref) : href;
72	};

Step C1 complete. Report follows.

## Bottom line

Three new files exist, each pure, each isomorphic where the plan required it, each covered by its own test file that I proved actually pins the behaviour (not just decorates it) by breaking it on purpose six times and watching it fail before reverting. Nothing outside `overrides/app/utils/` was touched — no dependency install, no config, no theme. Gates are clean: `tsc` exit 0, test suite 82 files / 1228 tests / 0 failures (up from a **verified** 79/1190 baseline I captured myself before writing anything, not the plan's stale 78-file assumption — more on that below).

## Files changed (all six new, all untracked, nothing else touched)

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts` (168 lines) + `.test.ts` (125 lines, 21 tests)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/crossSiteUrl.ts` (96 lines) + `.test.ts` (104 lines, 6 tests)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` (92 lines) + `.test.ts` (82 lines, 11 tests)

`git status --porcelain` shows exactly these six as `??`, nothing staged, nothing else modified.

### `regionPrefCookie.ts`
Split pure (`parseRegionPrefCookie`, `serialiseRegionPrefCookieValue`, `serialiseRegionPrefCookie`) from client-only (`getRegionPrefCookie`, `setRegionPrefCookie`) exactly as specified. Exports `COOKIE_NAME`, `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS = 7`. No `s` flag — and since `RegionPrefCookieValue`'s type has no `s` field at all, that's a compile-time guarantee, not just a runtime behaviour I have to keep re-testing. One number I had to invent that the plan left as `<long>`: cookie `max-age` is 400 days (the practical ceiling most browsers now enforce on cookie lifetime), deliberately *not* tied to `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS` — see "What Marcel is missing" below, this has a real interaction with SFCC-823 that's worth knowing about now.

### `crossSiteUrl.ts`
Reuses `getParamsFromPath` + `removeBasePathFromPath` (from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/site-utils`) and `getRouterBasePath` (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/utils`) exactly as the corrected prompt said was safe — verified myself by reading `site-utils.js` in full, not just trusting the citation.

### `shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts`
Pure predicate, discriminated-union return type (`{show:true, targetLanguage}` | `{show:false}` — per `typescript.md`'s own guidance on variant modelling, since the field only exists in one branch). Gate constant `EU_DOMESTIC_SFCC_SITE_ID = 'ZimmermannEU'` and `SUPPORTED_EU_LANGUAGES = ['en','fr','it','es']` verified against `config/sites.overlay.js:39-42` directly, not carried through from the prompt unchecked.

## Two deviations from the prompt's suggested design — both within the "adjust and justify" latitude I was given, flagging them anyway since they change what C3 will need to call

**1. `crossSiteUrl`'s signature dropped the leading `path: string` parameter.** Suggested signature was `crossSiteUrl(path, targetAlias, targetLocale, buildUrl, opts?)`. I read `getPathWithLocale` in full (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:118-119`): its real signature is `(shortCode, buildUrl, opts)` — the current path is *never* a separate argument, it always comes from `opts.location ?? window.location`. A `path` argument sitting alongside `opts.location.pathname` would just be the same value asserted twice with no rule for what happens if they disagree. I dropped it and mirrored the real function's shape exactly: **`crossSiteUrl(targetAlias, targetLocale, buildUrl, opts?)`** — 4 arguments, not 5. This matters concretely for whoever builds C3 next: that's the call shape to use.

**2. I did not import `getSiteByReference`**, despite the prompt listing it as safe. I read it (`site-utils.js:87-96`) and confirmed it resolves by alias correctly, as asked — but tracing *why* `getPathWithLocale` calls it (only to look up a *locale object* within the current site, via `getLocaleByReference`) showed it's not needed here: our target site/locale are already-known strings handed straight to `buildUrl`, untouched — the same "receives a target identifier and hands it back untouched" contract `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch`'s own props already use. Not importing it is less coupling to global site config for no loss of correctness.

Both are demonstrated working, not just argued: `crossSiteUrl.test.ts`'s 6 tests all pass against real `getParamsFromPath`/`removeBasePathFromPath` logic (mocked `getConfig` with real Zimmermann EU site data, following the vendor's own `url.test.js` mocking technique), including base-path-and-site-alias stripping together.

## Cross-cutting pass criteria — evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 | Ran clean before writing tests, and again at the end: exit 0, no output, both times |
| `npm run test` → 0 failures, count up by 6 | Baseline (captured myself first, per instruction not to assume a stale number): **79 files / 1190 tests**. Final: **82 files / 1228 tests, 0 failures**. Plan predicted 81/78+3 — that number was computed against the plan's own assumed 78-file baseline, which was already stale by the time I started (A1/A2/B1/B2 had landed at 79, not 78). Per the plan's own "Unverified gaps" section, "0 failures and the count strictly increasing" is the real bar, not the exact integer — both hold. |
| Zero `js-cookie` import | `grep -rn "js-cookie"` across all six files → no matches |
| `git diff --stat package.json package-lock.json` → empty | Confirmed empty |
| No `document` in the pure cookie functions | `grep -n document regionPrefCookie.ts` → every hit is either inside `getRegionPrefCookie`/`setRegionPrefCookie` or inside a JSDoc comment describing the *absence*; zero hits in `crossSiteUrl.ts`/`shouldShowLanguagePrompt.ts` at all |
| No hook imports | `grep` across all three impl files → the only hit is a JSDoc comment citing `use-multi-site.js` as design rationale, not an import statement |
| Pure functions, no side effects | Confirmed by reading — no I/O, no mutation of arguments |

## The six red-then-green pairs (mandatory proof, all run for real — not asserted)

1. **regionPrefCookie** — `LANGUAGE_PROMPT_SUPPRESSION_DAYS toBe(7)` → inverted to `toBe(8)` → **red** (`expected 7 to be 8`) → reverted → **green** (21/21).
2. **regionPrefCookie** — round-trip `toEqual(value)` → inverted `languageSuppressedAt` by +1 → **red** (`1700000000` received vs `1700000001` expected) → reverted → **green** (21/21).
3. **crossSiteUrl** — `expect(result).toBe('/fr-eu/product/123')` → inverted to `/999` → **red** → reverted → **green** (6/6).
4. **crossSiteUrl** — base-path-stripped assertion `toBe('/product/123')` → inverted to expect the base path still present → **red** → reverted → **green** (6/6).
5. **shouldShowLanguagePrompt** — window-lapsed branch (explicitly flagged by the plan as one of "the two that would pass trivially against a stub") → inverted expected from `{show:true, targetLanguage:'fr'}` to `{show:false}` → **red** → reverted → **green** (11/11).
6. **shouldShowLanguagePrompt** — `fr-FR`→`fr` primary-subtag match (the other plan-flagged case) → inverted expected to `{show:true,...}` (what an exact-string-equality stub would wrongly produce) → **red** → reverted → **green** (11/11).

Final confirmation after all reverts: `grep INVERTED-FOR-PROOF` → no matches left in any file; full suite → 82 files / 1228 tests / 0 failures; `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.

## Unverified gaps (mine)

- I did not run `npm run lint` or `npm run audit:tokens` for this step — neither is in C1's own pass-criteria list (unlike C3's), and `audit:tokens` only scans `overrides/app/components/**`/`overrides/app/theme/components/**`, which this step never touches. Skipped deliberately, not overlooked.
- `browserLanguages[0]`-only (not scanning the full preference list) is my own interpretive call on an underspecified corner the plan's six branches never exercise either way — documented in the code, doesn't affect any required test outcome, but is a real behavioural choice nobody explicitly signed off.
- I haven't run this against a real browser/Safari private-mode session — the throw-survival tests simulate the documented WebKit behaviour via `Object.defineProperty`, not a real Safari instance.

## What Marcel is missing

The `regionPrefCookie.ts` I just built will also carry the **country**-prompt timestamp (`c`) once SFCC-823 lands, sharing this file's one `max-age`. I set that to 400 days (a sensible finite ceiling for the *language* prompt's 7-day suppression window) — but the plan's own open question #1 says the country prompt's REG-019 requirement is "indefinite," not time-boxed. If SFCC-823 writes `c` to this same cookie without revisiting `max-age`, a shopper who explicitly dismissed the country prompt "forever" will quietly get asked again after ~13 months, contradicting REG-019 — a decision this step had to make (a number had to go somewhere) but shouldn't silently settle for a story I'm not building.
